translation:
This notice reached the province of Hai Zhou, where there was a man named Chen, whose given name was E and courtesy name was Guang Rui. Upon seeing the notice, he immediately went home and told his mother, Zhang, "The imperial court has released the Yellow List, announcing the opening of the Southern Province examination, seeking out talented individuals. I intend to go and take the examination. Should I be fortunate enough to obtain an official post, even a minor one, it will bring honor to our family, allow me to provide for my wife and children, and bring glory to our household. This is what I, your son, aspire to. I am informing you beforehand." Zhang replied, "My son, as a scholar, 'to learn in youth, to act in maturity' is indeed the proper path. But when you go to take the examination, be careful on your journey. When you gain an official position, come back home early." Guang Rui then instructed his servant to pack his belongings, bowed respectfully to his mother, and set off.

Upon reaching Chang'an, he arrived just as the examination hall was opened. After completing the examination and passing the imperial court's three-essay test, he was personally awarded the top ranking by the Tang Emperor, who bestowed upon him the privilege of riding through the streets for three days. Unexpectedly, as he rode past the residence of the Minister of State, Yin Kai Shan, he came across Yin Kai Shan's daughter, named Wen Jiao, also known as 'Full Hall's Jewel', who was unmarried and preparing for a matchmaking ceremony on her high platform, throwing a silk ball to choose her husband. It happened that Chen Guang Rui was passing by below. The young lady, upon seeing Guang Rui's extraordinary talent and recognizing him as the newly appointed top scholar, felt a deep affection for him. She tossed the silk ball down, which landed precisely on Guang Rui's official hat. Immediately, a festive fanfare and music filled the air, and a dozen maidservants descended from the platform, seizing Guang Rui's horse's reins and welcoming the top scholar into the minister's residence for marriage. The minister and his wife emerged from the hall, summoning their guests to witness the ceremony, and promptly paired their daughter with Guang Rui. After offering their respects to heaven and earth, the newly married couple bowed to each other, followed by a bow to their in-laws. The minister instructed for a banquet to be arranged, and they celebrated throughout the night.

translation:
When this proclamation reached the region of Haizhou, there was a man surnamed Chen, given name E, with the courtesy name Guangrui. Upon seeing the proclamation, he immediately went home and told his mother, Lady Zhang, "The imperial court has issued the Yellow List, announcing the opening of the Southern examination, seeking out talented individuals. I intend to go and take the exam. Should I be fortunate enough to obtain an official position, it will bring honor to our family, and allow me to provide for my wife and children, illuminating our household lineage. This is my ambition, Mother. I inform you of this beforehand." Lady Zhang said, "My son, as a scholar, 'to study in youth, to act in maturity' is as it should be. But when you go for the examination, be careful on your journey. Once you obtain an official post, return home as soon as possible." Guangrui then instructed his servant to pack his belongings, bowed in farewell to his mother, and hurried on his way. Upon arriving in Chang'an, it happened to be the time when the selection grounds were open. Guangrui immediately entered the examination hall. After passing the examinations, he was selected and then passed the three essays, receiving a first-rank appointment from the Tang emperor, who personally wrote his imperial decree and allowed him to ride a horse through the streets for three days.

Unintentionally, during his procession, he arrived at the gate of the Chancellor Yin Kaishan.  There, the Chancellor's daughter, named Wenjiao, also known as Mantangjiao, an unmarried woman, was holding a matchmaking ceremony, throwing an embroidered ball to choose her husband.  Just as Chen Guangrui passed by the building, the young miss saw him, recognizing his distinguished appearance and knowing he was the newly appointed top scholar, her heart filled with delight. She threw the embroidered ball downwards, and it landed precisely on Guangrui's scholar's hat. Suddenly, a festive ensemble of music and delicate melodies filled the air. Ten or so maidservants descended from the building, seizing Guangrui's horse's reins and welcoming the top scholar into the Chancellor's mansion for a betrothal. The Chancellor and his wife immediately came out to greet him, calling upon guests to offer congratulations. The young miss was then matched with Guangrui. After bowing to heaven and earth, and then to each other, they bowed to their future in-laws. The Chancellor ordered a banquet to be prepared, and they feasted throughout the night.

When this notice arrived in Haizhou, a man named Chen, whose given name was E and whose courtesy name was Guangrui, saw it and immediately went home. He told his mother, Zhang, “The imperial court has posted the yellow list, declaring the opening of the South Province examination to select talented officials. I intend to go and take the examination. If I am fortunate enough to obtain a post, I will be able to honor our family, raise our status, provide for my wife and children, and bring glory to our ancestors. This is my ambition. I inform you of this so you may know.” 

Zhang said, “My son, you are a scholar, learning in youth and taking action in maturity; this is indeed as it should be. But when you go to take the examination, be careful on the road. Once you have obtained an official position, return home as soon as possible.” Guangrui then instructed his servant to pack his belongings, bowed to his mother, and set off.

He arrived in Chang'an just as the examination was in full swing and entered the hall. After completing the examinations and passing the imperial examinations, he was granted the highest honor, the title of Number One Scholar, by the Tang Emperor. He rode through the streets for three days.

Unforeseen, as he rode past the house of the prime minister, Yin Kaisan, a daughter of the prime minister named Wenjiao, also known as Man Tangjiao, who had not yet been married, was hosting a high-profile matchmaking event on a decorated balcony. Guangrui, passing below, was recognized as the newly crowned Number One Scholar. The young lady was greatly pleased and, throwing a flower ball as part of the matchmaking ritual, struck Guangrui's hat. The sound of music and celebrations filled the air. Ten or so maidservants descended from the balcony, taking hold of Guangrui's horse, leading him into the prime minister's residence to wed.

The prime minister and his wife immediately emerged from the hall, called for musicians, and arranged for the ceremony. The young lady and Guangrui bowed to heaven and earth, then bowed to each other as husband and wife, before bowing to their respective parents-in-law. The prime minister ordered a grand feast to be prepared and they celebrated through the night.

He then followed the Executioner and with him entered the gate. The Executioner saw a horse inside the gate, already saddled, and urged the emperor to mount it. When the Executioner had helped him up, the horse went off like an arrow and soon arrived at the banks of the Wei River. In the water were a pair of golden carp playing together. At this sight the emperor was delighted, stopped the horse and seemed as if he would never tire of watching them. The Executioner said, “Your Majesty had better let the horse go on, so that we may enter the city early.” But the emperor was loath to leave the spot. The Executioner then gave the horse a kick and shouted out, “Why do you not go, what are you waiting for?” With this he gave a push, and the horse plunged into the Wei River, and thus the emperor left the territory of Hell, and returned among living men. At that time both the civil and military officials were gathered together about the heir, and the Empress Dowager and palace ladies were at the White Tiger Hall, weeping, and discussing how to put forth an edict about the emperor’s death, so as to inform the whole empire, and announce the accession of the heir to the throne. But Minister Wei said, “Let us wait one day more before doing this, as the emperor’s soul is sure to return to his body.”
human_translations.translator_3: When a gentleman called Guangrui from Haizhou learned of the imminent exam session, he immediately asked his mother’s permission to attend. “If I were lucky enough to earn an official posting, it would enhance our family’s reputation, and benefit my future wife and sons.” “You’re ready for this,” his mother—a lady surnamed Zhang—agreed. “But take care, and come back as soon as you’ve been given a job.” Guangrui reached Chang’an just in time for the start of the exams and, when the results came out, discovered that he had come in first. After receiving a certificate signed by the emperor himself, he was toured on horseback through the streets of the capital for three whole days. The procession passed by the house of Yin Kaishan, one of Taizong’s chief ministers, who had a captivatingly pretty, unmarried daughter called Wenjiao. At the very moment that Guangrui passed beneath, Wenjiao was about to drop an embroidered ball from a decorated tower; whomever it chanced to hit would be her husband. The moment she laid eyes on Guangrui, Wenjiao could see that he was an exceptional young man, a first impression corroborated by his ranking top in the civil service exam. Not coincidentally, the embroidered ball scored a direct hit against Guangrui’s black silk hat. A symphony of pipes and flutes erupted, and an army of maidservants rushed out of the building, grabbed the bridle of Guangrui’s horse, and welcomed the examination star into the house of his future in-laws. Yin Kaishan and his wife immediately summoned guests and a master of ceremonies, and married the young lady off to Guangrui. The new couple bowed to heaven and earth, to each other, and to the girl’s parents. The minister gave a huge banquet and, after an evening’s revelry, the new couple retired hand in hand to the bridal chamber.
human_translations.translator_4: When this notice reached the district of Haizhou it was seen by a man called Chen E, whose courtesy name was Guangrui. He returned home and said to Madame Zhang, his mother, “The court has issued a yellow notice saying that the Chancellery will be opened for an examination to select men of wisdom and talent. Your child wants to go and take part. Such is my ambition; and I have come to tell you, mother, that I am going.” “You are a scholar, my son,” his mother replied, “and it is right that 'one who studies when young should travel when grown up'. But do take care on the journey to the examinations, and if you are given office, come back home as soon as you can.” Chen Guangrui then ordered his servants to get his luggage together, took his leave of his mother, and started off on his journey. When he reached Chang'an the examination grounds were open and he went in. Having been successful in this examination, he went to the palace for the three questions test. The Tang Emperor personally awarded him the first place, and he was paraded round the streets on horseback for three days. It happened that just when the procession was passing the gateway of the minister Yin Kaishan, the minister's unmarried daughter Wenqiao, whose other name was Man-tang-qiao (Beauty Throughout the Hall), was making decorations for the house and throwing an embroidered ball to see who her future husband would be. When Chen Guangrui passed below she saw at once that he was exceptionally handsome, and she knew that he had come first in the recent examinations. She was thoroughly taken with him, and when she dropped her embroidered ball it landed squarely on his black hat. To the sound of pipes and flutes a dozen or so maidservants and serving women hurried downstairs to take hold of the head of Chen Guangrui's horse and invite him into the minister's mansion to marry his daughter. The minister and his wife came into the main hall, and when they had called for a master of ceremonies they married their daughter to Guangrui. When bride and groom had bowed to Heaven, Earth and each other they both bowed to the bride's father and mother. The minister ordered a banquet, and there was a night of drinking and celebration.

translation:
Three years had passed, and the Master ascended the sacred seat once more to discourse with the multitude. He spoke of paradoxical sayings and debated the encompassing nature of appearances. He suddenly asked, “Where is Wukong?” Wukong stepped forward and knelt, saying, “Disciple is here.” The Master said, “What path have you been cultivating all this while?” Wukong replied, “Disciple's understanding of the Dharma nature has become profound, and the roots have also grown firm.” The Master said, “Since you have grasped the Dharma nature and gained a solid foundation, you have entered the state of embodied spirit, yet you are merely guarding against the ‘three calamities.’” Hearing this, Wukong pondered for a long time before saying, “Master, your words are amiss. I often hear that those of great virtue and high attainment live as long as Heaven, traversing fire and water unscathed, immune to a hundred diseases. How can there be these ‘three calamities’?” The Master said, “This is an exceptional path: one that defies the natural order of Heaven and Earth, encroaching upon the profound mysteries of sun and moon. After the elixir is perfected, even gods and spirits cannot abide. Though your appearance may remain youthful for millennia, after five hundred years, a thunderbolt will descend from Heaven, striking you. You must see into your true nature and clear your mind to escape. If you evade it, you will live as long as Heaven; if you fail, you will meet your end. Another five hundred years later, a fire will descend from Heaven. This fire is not heavenly fire, nor is it ordinary fire; it is called ‘Yin fire.’ It will erupt from the base of your spine and scorch through your palace of bones, turning your five organs to ash and your limbs to decay, rendering all your millennia of arduous practice hollow. And finally, after another five hundred years, a wind calamity will befall you. This wind is not the winds of the four cardinal directions, nor the wind that blows incense and gold, nor the wind that rustles flowers, willows, pines, or bamboo; it is called ‘Bi wind.’ It will blow in from the fontanelle and pass through your six internal organs, the dantian, and the nine orifices, causing your bones and flesh to wither away until your body dissolves. Therefore, you must all evade these calamities.”

Upon hearing this, Wukong trembled with fear and bowed deeply, saying, “Great Master, you have shown mercy by revealing the method of escaping the three calamities. I dare not forget your kindness.”

The Master said, “This is not difficult, but your circumstances are different from others, so I cannot pass it on to you.” Wukong said, “I have a rounded head that reaches the sky, feet that cover the earth, and the same nine orifices, four limbs, five organs, and six internal organs as humans. How can I be different?”

The Master said, “Though you resemble a human, you lack cheeks.” Wukong realized his cheekbones were flat and his face was narrow and pointed. He touched his face and laughed, “Master, you haven’t outsmarted me! Although I lack cheeks, I have this pouch that you don’t have, which can also serve as a substitute.”

The Master said, “Very well, if you wish to learn like an ordinary human, there are thirty-six Heavenly transformations and seventy-two Earthly transformations.”

Wukong said, “Disciple wishes to learn one Earthly transformation.”

The Master said, “Very well, come forward, and I will teach you the incantations.” He then whispered something in Wukong’s ear. This monkey king was someone who understood things instantly. After hearing the incantations, he practiced diligently, and in no time, mastered all seventy-two Earthly transformations.
source_text: 却早过了三年，祖师复登宝座，与众说法。谈的是公案比语，论的是外像包皮。忽问：“悟空何在？”悟空近前跪下：“弟子有。”祖师道：“你这一向修些什么道来？”悟空道：“弟子近来法性颇通，根源亦渐坚固矣。”祖师道：“你既通法性，会得根源，已注神体，却只是防备着‘三灾利害’。”悟空听说，沉吟良久道：“师父之言谬矣。我常闻道高德隆，与天同寿，水火既济，百病不生，却怎么有个三灾利害？”祖师道：“此乃非常之道：夺天地之造化，侵日月之玄机；丹成之后，鬼神难容。虽驻颜益寿，但到了五百年后，天降雷灾打你，须要见性明心，预先躲避。躲得过，寿与天齐，躲不过，就此绝命。再五百年后，天降火灾烧你。这火不是天火，亦不是凡火，唤做‘阴火’。自本身涌泉穴下烧起，直透泥垣宫，五脏成灰，四肢皆朽，把千年苦行，俱为虚幻。再五百年，又降风灾吹你。这风不是东南西北风，不是和薰金朔风，亦不是花柳松竹风，唤做‘赑风’。自囟门中吹入六腑，过丹田，穿九窍，骨肉消疏，其身自解。所以都要躲过。”悟空闻说，毛骨悚然，叩头礼拜道：“万老爷垂悯，传与躲避三灾之法，到底不敢忘恩。”祖师道：“此亦无难，只是你比他人不同，故传不得。”悟空道：“我也头圆顶天，足方履地，一般有九窍四肢，五脏六腑，何以比人不同？”祖师道：“你虽然像人，却比人少腮。”原来那猴子孤拐面，凹脸尖嘴。悟空伸手一摸，笑道：“师父没成算！我虽少腮，却比人多这个素袋，亦可准折过也。”祖师说：“也罢，你要学那一般？有一般天罡数，该三十六般变化，有一般地煞数，该七十二般变化。”悟空道：“弟子愿多里捞摸，学一个地煞变化罢。”祖师道：“既如此，上前来，传与你口诀。”遂附耳低言，不知说了些甚么妙法。这猴王也是一窍通时百窍通，当时习了口诀，自修自炼，将七十二般变化，都学成了。

human_translations.translator_1: Three years went by swiftly, and the Patriarch again mounted his throne to lecture to the multitude. He discussed the scholastic deliberations and parables, and he discoursed on the integument of external conduct. Suddenly he asked, “Where’s Wukong?” Wukong drew near and knelt down. “Your pupil’s here,” he said. “What sort of art have you been practicing lately?” the Patriarch asked. “Recently,” Wukong said, “your pupil has begun to apprehend the nature of all things and my foundational knowledge has become firmly established.” “If you have penetrated to the dharma nature to apprehend the origin,” said the Patriarch, “you have, in fact, entered into the divine substance. You need, however, to guard against the danger of three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, he thought for a long time and said, “The words of the master must be erroneous. I have frequently heard that when one is learned in the Way and excels in virtue, he will enjoy the same age as Heaven; fire and water cannot harm him and every kind of disease will vanish. How can there be this danger of three calamities?” “What you have learned,” said the Patriarch, “is no ordinary magic: you have stolen the creative powers of Heaven and Earth and invaded the dark mysteries of the sun and moon. Your success in perfecting the elixir is something that the gods and the demons cannot countenance. Though your appearance will be preserved and your age lengthened, after five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of thunder to strike you. Hence you must be intelligent and wise enough to avoid it ahead of time. If you can escape it, your age will indeed equal that of Heaven; if not, your life will thus be finished. After another five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of fire to burn you. That fire is neither natural nor common fire; its name is the Fire of Yin, and it arises from within the soles of your feet to reach even the cavity of your heart, reducing your entrails to ashes and your limbs to utter ruin. The arduous labor of a millennium will then have been made completely superfluous. After another five hundred years the calamity of wind will be sent to blow at you. It is not the wind from the north, south, east, or west; nor is it one of the winds of four seasons; nor is it the wind of flowers, willows, pines, and bamboos. It is called the Mighty Wind, and it enters from the top of the skull into the body, passes through the midriff, and penetrates the nine apertures.12 The bones and the flesh will be dissolved and the body itself will disintegrate. You must therefore avoid all three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, his hairs stood on end, and, kowtowing reverently, he said, “I beg the master to be merciful and impart to me the method to avoid the three calamities. To the very end, I shall never forget your gracious favor.” The Patriarch said, “It is not, in fact, difficult, except that I cannot teach you because you are somewhat different from other people.” “I have a round head pointing to Heaven,” said Wukong, “and square feet walking on Earth. Similarly, I have nine apertures and four limbs, entrails and cavities. In what way am I different from other people?” The Patriarch said, “Though you resemble a man, you have much less jowl.” The monkey, you see, has an angular face with hollow cheeks and a pointed mouth. Stretching his hand to feel himself, Wukong laughed and said, “The master does not know how to balance matters! Though I have much less jowl than human beings, I have my pouch, which may certainly be considered a compensation.” “Very well, then,” said the Patriarch, “what method of escape would you like to learn? There is the Art of the Heavenly Ladle, which numbers thirty-six transformations, and there is the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which numbers seventy-two transformations.” Wukong said, “Your pupil is always eager to catch more fishes, so I’ll learn the Art of the Earthly Multitude.” “In that case,” said the Patriarch, “come up here, and I’ll pass on the oral formulas to you.” He then whispered something into his ear, though we do not know what sort of wondrous secrets he spoke of. But this Monkey King was someone who, knowing one thing, could understand a hundred! He immediately learned the oral formulas and, after working at them and practicing them himself, he mastered all seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_2: The Seeker of Secrets, having learnt the three secrets of Immortality: mind and spirit and abstinence from sex, memorized these carefully, and went on studying alone for three years more. Then the Master again mounted the platform and preached on the Parable of the Great Judgment. Suddenly he asked, “Where is the Seeker of Secrets?” The Monkey King came forward, knelt and said, “I am here.” The Master asked, “What have you been learning all this time?” “Your disciple has mastered the study of the spiritual nature.” The Master said, “Then you know the origin of things. But you must be careful of three great dangers.” The Seeker of Secrets, after pondering over this for a long time said, “I have constantly heard it said that when one has found Truth and Virtue, then one becomes an Immortal and no sickness can befall him; how then do you speak of dangers to be avoided?” The Master said, “What I teach you is not an ordinary doctrine, for it controls the forces of Heaven and Earth and the secrets of the sun, moon, and stars. When one has arrived at this stage, then one is superior to the evil spirits and the ordinary gods. Still after a time there will come a thunderclap to try your soul and spirit. If unmoved and unshaken in the deluge, you will be like Heaven itself. If you doubt, then you perish. After a long practice of religion again, one is tried a second time. This danger does not come from Heaven, nor from man, but from one’s own passions. It burns one’s whole body to ashes, and all one’s long years of practice are in vain like a dream. After another long term of practice, one is tried a third time by the danger of environment, which blows on one like a typhoon and affects one’s whole being. This must be overcome.” When the Seeker of Secrets heard this his body shook and his hair stood on end. “Oh Master, have pity on me, and tell me how to overcome these three dangers, and I shall never forget your kindness.” The Master said, “That is not difficult. There are two ways to avoid them. One has 36 wonders, the other 72; which do you wish to know?” The Seeker of Secrets said, “I wish to know the 72 wonders.” “Come here then, and I will teach you the incantation.” Then he whispered it in his ear. The Monkey King felt influences going through every pore of his body, and began to practice the arts and to learn the whole 72 wonders.
human_translations.translator_3: Another three years passed before Subodhi reappeared to teach his disciples. He spoke of academic debates and parables and of external self-cultivation. “Where’s Monkey?” he suddenly asked. Monkey kneeled before him. “Here I am!” “What have you been working on of late?” “The basics of immortality: the nature and origins of all things.” “In that case, you have already penetrated the divine substance of matter. But beware of the peril of the three calamities.” Monkey mulled this over for a while. “Master is surely mistaken,” he eventually responded. “I thought that anyone who has learned the Way and is rich in virtue will live as long as Heaven itself. Neither fire, nor water, nor illness can harm him. What three calamities do you speak of?” “What you have learned is not ordinary magic. You have stolen the creative power of heaven and earth itself, and penetrated the dark formulae of the sun and the moon. Ghosts and spirits will seek to bring you down. Although you have extended your life, in five hundred years’ time Heaven will unleash the calamity of thunder at you. You must seek wisdom to prevent this peril. Succeed and you will live as long as Heaven itself. Fail and you will die. In another five hundred years, Heaven will rain the calamity of the cold, dark fire of yin. It burns from the soles of your feet to the cavity of your heart. It will reduce your entrails to ashes and your limbs to ruins. Your millennium of hard work will then be as dust and nothingness. After another five hundred years, Heaven will set the calamity of wind onto you. This is no earthly wind. It enters through the fontanels, blows through the six internal organs, midriff, and nine orifices. Your flesh and bones will dissolve and your body will disintegrate. You see, then, why I recommend avoiding these calamities.” Monkey’s fur stood on end. “Tell me how to escape these horrors!” “Normally, this would be perfectly simple. But as you are an unusual specimen, I fear I cannot teach you.” “I’ve a head at the top and feet at the bottom, nine apertures, four limbs, five viscera, and six internal organs. How am I unusual?” “You bear a superficial resemblance to humans, but your cheeks are abnormally flat.” (Monkeys have rather angular faces, with sunken cheeks and pointed muzzles.) Monkey patted his face combatively. “Appearances can be deceptive. My cheek pouches have storage capacity on the inside. I demand parity.” “Fair enough,” considered Subodhi. “Which escape do you want to learn? There’s the Art of the Big Dipper, which involves thirty-six transformations, or the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which involves seventy-two.” “The more the merrier,” considered Monkey. “I’ll take the second.” “Come over here, then, and I will tell you the formula.” No one knows what Subodhi whispered into Monkey’s ear. But our hero was someone who could learn a hundred things from a single explanation. He immediately memorized the magic and, after practicing on his own, mastered the seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_4: After three years had passed in this way the Patriarch once more sat on his lecturing throne and expounded the Dharma to the students. He recounted famous sayings and parables, and discussed external phenomena and external appearances. Without warning he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong went forward, knelt down and replied, “Your disciple is present.” “What Way have you cultivated since coming here?” “Your disciple is now fairly well conversant with the Dharma,” Sun Wukong replied, “and my Source is getting gradually stronger.” “If you are conversant with the Dharma and you know about the Source,” the Patriarch replied, “and if the spirit has already flowed into you, then you must beware of the 'Three Disasters.'” Sun Wukong thought for a long time, then he said, “Patriarch, you're talking rubbish. I have often heard that the Way is lofty and its power mighty, that it is as eternal as Heaven, that it can overcome fire and water, and prevent all illnesses from arising, so how could there be “Three Disasters?'” To this the Patriarch replied, “This is not the ordinary Way: it involves seizing the very creation of Heaven and Earth, and encroaching on the hidden workings of the sun and moon. Once the elixir is made, devils and spirits cannot tolerate it. Although it will preserve the youthfulness of your face and prolong your life, in five hundred years' time Heaven will strike you with a thunderbolt. You must be clear-sighted in nature and mind, so that you can hide from it before it comes. If you succeed in avoiding it you will live as long as Heaven; and if you don't, it will kill you. Another five hundred years later Heaven will burn you with fire. This fire will be not heavenly fire or ordinary fire but 'hidden fire'. It will burn you from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head; your five viscera will be reduced to ashes, your four limbs will be destroyed, and a thousand years of asceticism will have been so much wasted time. Yet another five hundred years later a wind will blow at you. It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? The Monkey King was the sort of person who understands everything once he is told a tiny part, and he learned the spells on the spot. He practiced and trained until he had mastered all seventy-two transformations.

It blows in from the fontanelle and sweeps through the six internal organs, passes through the dantian, pierces the nine apertures, causing the bones and flesh to disperse, and the body to dissolve.

Wukong, upon hearing this, felt a chill down his spine. He bowed deeply and said, "Lord, your benevolence is immeasurable, to have shared the method of avoiding the three calamities. I dare not forget your grace."

The master said, "This is not difficult. However, you are different from others, so I cannot pass it on."

Wukong said, "I too have a round head that touches the sky, and feet that cover the earth. I have nine apertures, four limbs, five internal organs, and six bowels. How am I different from others?"

The master said, "Although you resemble humans, you lack the cheeks."

It turned out that the monkey had a sharp, concave face with a pointed mouth. Wukong reached out and touched his face, and laughed, "Master, you've missed! Though I lack cheeks, I have this pouch, which I can also use to avert the calamity."

The master said, "Very well, if you wish to learn like ordinary people, there is a celestial calculation called the Thirty-Six Transformations of Heaven and an earthly calculation called the Seventy-Two Transformations. You wish to learn the Seventy-Two Transformations?"

Wukong said, "Disciple wishes to learn one transformation from the earthly calculation."

The master said, "Very well, come forward and I will pass on the incantations." He then leaned close and whispered something unintelligible. That monkey king had the ability to understand immediately. He learned the incantations and began his own practice, ultimately mastering all seventy-two transformations.

human_translations.translator_1: Three years went by swiftly, and the Patriarch again mounted his throne to lecture to the multitude. He discussed the scholastic deliberations and parables, and he discoursed on the integument of external conduct. Suddenly he asked, “Where’s Wukong?” Wukong drew near and knelt down. “Your pupil’s here,” he said. “What sort of art have you been practicing lately?” the Patriarch asked. “Recently,” Wukong said, “your pupil has begun to apprehend the nature of all things and my foundational knowledge has become firmly established.” “If you have penetrated to the dharma nature to apprehend the origin,” said the Patriarch, “you have, in fact, entered into the divine substance. You need, however, to guard against the danger of three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, he thought for a long time and said, “The words of the master must be erroneous. I have frequently heard that when one is learned in the Way and excels in virtue, he will enjoy the same age as Heaven; fire and water cannot harm him and every kind of disease will vanish. How can there be this danger of three calamities?” “What you have learned,” said the Patriarch, “is no ordinary magic: you have stolen the creative powers of Heaven and Earth and invaded the dark mysteries of the sun and moon. Your success in perfecting the elixir is something that the gods and the demons cannot countenance. Though your appearance will be preserved and your age lengthened, after five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of thunder to strike you. Hence you must be intelligent and wise enough to avoid it ahead of time. If you can escape it, your age will indeed equal that of Heaven; if not, your life will thus be finished. After another five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of fire to burn you. That fire is neither natural nor common fire; its name is the Fire of Yin, and it arises from within the soles of your feet to reach even the cavity of your heart, reducing your entrails to ashes and your limbs to utter ruin. The arduous labor of a millennium will then have been made completely superfluous. After another five hundred years the calamity of wind will be sent to blow at you. It is not the wind from the north, south, east, or west; nor is it one of the winds of four seasons; nor is it the wind of flowers, willows, pines, and bamboos. It is called the Mighty Wind, and it enters from the top of the skull into the body, passes through the midriff, and penetrates the nine apertures.12 The bones and the flesh will be dissolved and the body itself will disintegrate. You must therefore avoid all three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, his hairs stood on end, and, kowtowing reverently, he said, “I beg the master to be merciful and impart to me the method to avoid the three calamities. To the very end, I shall never forget your gracious favor.” The Patriarch said, “It is not, in fact, difficult, except that I cannot teach you because you are somewhat different from other people.” “I have a round head pointing to Heaven,” said Wukong, “and square feet walking on Earth. Similarly, I have nine apertures and four limbs, entrails and cavities. In what way am I different from other people?” The Patriarch said, “Though you resemble a man, you have much less jowl.” The monkey, you see, has an angular face with hollow cheeks and a pointed mouth. Stretching his hand to feel himself, Wukong laughed and said, “The master does not know how to balance matters! Though I have much less jowl than human beings, I have my pouch, which may certainly be considered a compensation.” “Very well, then,” said the Patriarch, “what method of escape would you like to learn? There is the Art of the Heavenly Ladle, which numbers thirty-six transformations, and there is the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which numbers seventy-two transformations.” Wukong said, “Your pupil is always eager to catch more fishes, so I’ll learn the Art of the Earthly Multitude.” “In that case,” said the Patriarch, “come up here, and I’ll pass on the oral formulas to you.” He then whispered something into his ear, though we do not know what sort of wondrous secrets he spoke of. But this Monkey King was someone who, knowing one thing, could understand a hundred! He immediately learned the oral formulas and, after working at them and practicing them himself, he mastered all seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_2: The Seeker of Secrets, having learnt the three secrets of Immortality: mind and spirit and abstinence from sex, memorized these carefully, and went on studying alone for three years more. Then the Master again mounted the platform and preached on the Parable of the Great Judgment. Suddenly he asked, “Where is the Seeker of Secrets?” The Monkey King came forward, knelt and said, “I am here.” The Master asked, “What have you been learning all this time?” “Your disciple has mastered the study of the spiritual nature.” The Master said, “Then you know the origin of things. But you must be careful of three great dangers.” The Seeker of Secrets, after pondering over this for a long time said, “I have constantly heard it said that when one has found Truth and Virtue, then one becomes an Immortal and no sickness can befall him; how then do you speak of dangers to be avoided?” The Master said, “What I teach you is not an ordinary doctrine, for it controls the forces of Heaven and Earth and the secrets of the sun, moon, and stars. When one has arrived at this stage, then one is superior to the evil spirits and the ordinary gods. Still after a time there will come a thunderclap to try your soul and spirit. If unmoved and unshaken in the deluge, you will be like Heaven itself. If you doubt, then you perish. After a long practice of religion again, one is tried a second time. This danger does not come from Heaven, nor from man, but from one’s own passions. It burns one’s whole body to ashes, and all one’s long years of practice are in vain like a dream. After another long term of practice, one is tried a third time by the danger of environment, which blows on one like a typhoon and affects one’s whole being. This must be overcome.” When the Seeker of Secrets heard this his body shook and his hair stood on end. “Oh Master, have pity on me, and tell me how to overcome these three dangers, and I shall never forget your kindness.” The Master said, “That is not difficult. There are two ways to avoid them. One has 36 wonders, the other 72; which do you wish to know?” The Seeker of Secrets said, “I wish to know the 72 wonders.” “Come here then, and I will teach you the incantation.” Then he whispered it in his ear. The Monkey King felt influences going through every pore of his body, and began to practice the arts and to learn the whole 72 wonders.
human_translations.translator_3: Another three years passed before Subodhi reappeared to teach his disciples. He spoke of academic debates and parables and of external self-cultivation. “Where’s Monkey?” he suddenly asked. Monkey kneeled before him. “Here I am!” “What have you been working on of late?” “The basics of immortality: the nature and origins of all things.” “In that case, you have already penetrated the divine substance of matter. But beware of the peril of the three calamities.” Monkey mulled this over for a while. “Master is surely mistaken,” he eventually responded. “I thought that anyone who has learned the Way and is rich in virtue will live as long as Heaven itself. Neither fire, nor water, nor illness can harm him. What three calamities do you speak of?” “What you have learned is not ordinary magic. You have stolen the creative power of heaven and earth itself, and penetrated the dark formulae of the sun and the moon. Ghosts and spirits will seek to bring you down. Although you have extended your life, in five hundred years’ time Heaven will unleash the calamity of thunder at you. You must seek wisdom to prevent this peril. Succeed and you will live as long as Heaven itself. Fail and you will die. In another five hundred years, Heaven will rain the calamity of the cold, dark fire of yin. It burns from the soles of your feet to the cavity of your heart. It will reduce your entrails to ashes and your limbs to ruins. Your millennium of hard work will then be as dust and nothingness. After another five hundred years, Heaven will set the calamity of wind onto you. This is no earthly wind. It enters through the fontanels, blows through the six internal organs, midriff, and nine orifices. Your flesh and bones will dissolve and your body will disintegrate. You see, then, why I recommend avoiding these calamities.” Monkey’s fur stood on end. “Tell me how to escape these horrors!” “Normally, this would be perfectly simple. But as you are an unusual specimen, I fear I cannot teach you.” “I’ve a head at the top and feet at the bottom, nine apertures, four limbs, five viscera, and six internal organs. How am I unusual?” “You bear a superficial resemblance to humans, but your cheeks are abnormally flat.” (Monkeys have rather angular faces, with sunken cheeks and pointed muzzles.) Monkey patted his face combatively. “Appearances can be deceptive. My cheek pouches have storage capacity on the inside. I demand parity.” “Fair enough,” considered Subodhi. “Which escape do you want to learn? There’s the Art of the Big Dipper, which involves thirty-six transformations, or the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which involves seventy-two.” “The more the merrier,” considered Monkey. “I’ll take the second.” “Come over here, then, and I will tell you the formula.” No one knows what Subodhi whispered into Monkey’s ear. But our hero was someone who could learn a hundred things from a single explanation. He immediately memorized the magic and, after practicing on his own, mastered the seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_4: After three years had passed in this way the Patriarch once more sat on his lecturing throne and expounded the Dharma to the students. He recounted famous sayings and parables, and discussed external phenomena and external appearances. Without warning he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong went forward, knelt down and replied, “Your disciple is present.” “What Way have you cultivated since coming here?” “Your disciple is now fairly well conversant with the Dharma,” Sun Wukong replied, “and my Source is getting gradually stronger.” “If you are conversant with the Dharma and you know about the Source,” the Patriarch replied, “and if the spirit has already flowed into you, then you must beware of the 'Three Disasters.'” Sun Wukong thought for a long time, then he said, “Patriarch, you're talking rubbish. I have often heard that the Way is lofty and its power mighty, that it is as eternal as Heaven, that it can overcome fire and water, and prevent all illnesses from arising, so how could there be “Three Disasters?'” To this the Patriarch replied, “This is not the ordinary Way: it involves seizing the very creation of Heaven and Earth, and encroaching on the hidden workings of the sun and moon. Once the elixir is made, devils and spirits cannot tolerate it. Although it will preserve the youthfulness of your face and prolong your life, in five hundred years' time Heaven will strike you with a thunderbolt. You must be clear-sighted in nature and mind, so that you can hide from it before it comes. If you succeed in avoiding it you will live as long as Heaven; and if you don't, it will kill you. Another five hundred years later Heaven will burn you with fire. This fire will be not heavenly fire or ordinary fire but 'hidden fire'. It will burn you from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head; your five viscera will be reduced to ashes, your four limbs will be destroyed, and a thousand years of asceticism will have been so much wasted time. Yet another five hundred years later a wind will blow at you. It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? The Monkey King was the sort of person who understands everything once he is told a tiny part, and he learned the spells on the spot. He practiced and trained until he had mastered all seventy-two transformations.

translation:
Three years had passed, and the master ascended his throne again, lecturing the crowd. He spoke of cases and parables, discussing the outward form of the body. Suddenly, he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong approached and knelt down, saying, “Here I am, disciple.”

The master said, “What path have you been cultivating all this time?”

Sun Wukong replied, “My disciple has recently grasped the essence of the Dharma, and the foundation is gradually firming.”

The master said, “Since you’ve understood the essence of the Dharma and attained the source, you’ve already concentrated your spirit into your physical form, yet you’re only concerned with protecting yourself from the ‘three disasters and calamities’.”

Sun Wukong heard this and pondered for a long time, saying, “Master, your words are wrong. I’ve always heard that those of high virtue and enlightenment live as long as heaven and earth, safely traversing water and fire, immune to a hundred diseases. How can there be such a thing as the ‘three disasters and calamities’?”

The master said, “This is the path beyond the ordinary: defying the natural order of heaven and earth, violating the profound secrets of the sun and moon. After the elixir is perfected, even gods and spirits find it difficult to tolerate. Although it prolongs your appearance and lifespan, after five hundred years, a heavenly thunderclap will strike you down. You must then perceive your true nature and enlighten your mind beforehand to avoid it. If you manage to dodge it, you’ll live as long as heaven and earth; if not, your life will end here.

Five hundred years later, a fire calamity will descend from the heavens. This is no ordinary fire, but a ‘Yin fire’. It will erupt from the spring well at the base of your body, burning straight through your dwelling and reaching your palace, turning your five internal organs to ash and your limbs to dust, making a thousand years of ascetic practices seem like an illusion.

And five hundred years after that, a wind calamity will blow you away. This is not a wind from the east, south, west, or north, nor the wind that scents the gold and washes away the dust, nor the wind from the flowers, willows, pines, and bamboos. It is called ‘bi feng’. It will blow in from the fontanelle at the top of your head, through your six internal organs, over your dantian, through your nine orifices, dissolving your flesh and bones until your body falls apart.

Therefore, you must learn to avoid them all.”

Sun Wukong heard this, and his hair stood on end. He bowed his head and said, “Master, your grace spares me and teaches me the way to avoid the three calamities. I will never forget your kindness.”

The master said, “There is nothing difficult about this. It’s just that you are different from others, so I cannot teach you the same way.”

Sun Wukong said, “I have a round head, feet that touch the ground, and the same nine orifices, four limbs, and five internal organs as any man. How am I different?”

The master said, “Although you look human, you lack cheeks.” It turned out that the monkey had a sunken face with a pointed mouth. Sun Wukong reached out and touched his face, laughing, “Master, you’re mistaken! Although I lack cheeks, I have this fleshy pouch, which can also be used to change my appearance.”

The master said, “Well then, do you want to learn the same way? There are thirty-six transformations of heaven and seventy-two transformations of earth.”

Sun Wukong said, “Disciple is willing to put in the effort and learn one of the seventy-two earthly transformations.”

The master said, “If that’s the case, come forward, and I will teach you the formulas.” He leaned close and whispered something in his ear, revealing a secret method. 

The Monkey King was quick to understand. Having grasped one principle, he grasped them all. He immediately practiced and perfected all seventy-two earthly transformations.

Then the Master again mounted the platform and preached on the Parable of the Great Judgment. Suddenly he asked, “Where is the Seeker of Secrets?” The Monkey King came forward, knelt and said, “I am here.” The Master asked, “What have you been learning all this time?” “Your disciple has mastered the study of the spiritual nature.” The Master said, “Then you know the origin of things. When one has arrived at this stage, then one is superior to the evil spirits and the ordinary gods. Still after a time there will come a thunderclap to try your soul and spirit. If unmoved and unshaken in the deluge, you will be like Heaven itself. If you doubt, then you perish. After a long practice of religion again, one is tried a second time. This danger does not come from Heaven, nor from man, but from one’s own passions. It burns one’s whole body to ashes, and all one’s long years of practice are in vain like a dream. human_translations.translator_3: Another three years passed before Subodhi reappeared to teach his disciples. He spoke of academic debates and parables and of external self-cultivation. “Where’s Monkey?” he suddenly asked. Monkey kneeled before him. “Here I am!” “What have you been working on of late?” “The basics of immortality: the nature and origins of all things.” “In that case, you have already penetrated the divine substance of matter. But beware of the peril of the three calamities.” Monkey mulled this over for a while. “Master is surely mistaken,” he eventually responded. “I thought that anyone who has learned the Way and is rich in virtue will live as long as Heaven itself. Neither fire, nor water, nor illness can harm him. What three calamities do you speak of?” “What you have learned is not ordinary magic. You have stolen the creative power of heaven and earth itself, and penetrated the dark formulae of the sun and the moon. Ghosts and spirits will seek to bring you down. Although you have extended your life, in five hundred years’ time Heaven will unleash the calamity of thunder at you. You must seek wisdom to prevent this peril. Succeed and you will live as long as Heaven itself. Fail and you will die. In another five hundred years, Heaven will rain the calamity of the cold, dark fire of yin. It burns from the soles of your feet to the cavity of your heart. It will reduce your entrails to ashes and your limbs to ruins. Your millennium of hard work will then be as dust and nothingness. After another five hundred years, Heaven will set the calamity of wind onto you. This is no earthly wind. It enters through the fontanels, blows through the six internal organs, midriff, and nine orifices. Your flesh and bones will dissolve and your body will disintegrate. You see, then, why I recommend avoiding these calamities.” Monkey’s fur stood on end. “Tell me how to escape these horrors!” “Normally, this would be perfectly simple. But as you are an unusual specimen, I fear I cannot teach you.” “I’ve a head at the top and feet at the bottom, nine apertures, four limbs, five viscera, and six internal organs. How am I unusual?” “You bear a superficial resemblance to humans, but your cheeks are abnormally flat.” (Monkeys have rather angular faces, with sunken cheeks and pointed muzzles.) Monkey patted his face combatively. “Appearances can be deceptive. My cheek pouches have storage capacity on the inside. I demand parity.” “Fair enough,” considered Subodhi. “Which escape do you want to learn? There’s the Art of the Big Dipper, which involves thirty-six transformations, or the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which involves seventy-two.” “The more the merrier,” considered Monkey. “I’ll take the second.” “Come over here, then, and I will tell you the formula.” No one knows what Subodhi whispered into Monkey’s ear. But our hero was someone who could learn a hundred things from a single explanation. He immediately memorized the magic and, after practicing on his own, mastered the seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_4: After three years had passed in this way the Patriarch once more sat on his lecturing throne and expounded the Dharma to the students. He recounted famous sayings and parables, and discussed external phenomena and external appearances. Without warning he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong went forward, knelt down and replied, “Your disciple is present.” “What Way have you cultivated since coming here?” “Your disciple is now fairly well conversant with the Dharma,” Sun Wukong replied, “and my Source is getting gradually stronger.” “If you are conversant with the Dharma and you know about the Source,” the Patriarch replied, “and if the spirit has already flowed into you, then you must beware of the 'Three Disasters.'” Sun Wukong thought for a long time, then he said, “Patriarch, you're talking rubbish. I have often heard that the Way is lofty and its power mighty, that it is as eternal as Heaven, that it can overcome fire and water, and prevent all illnesses from arising, so how could there be “Three Disasters?'” To this the Patriarch replied, “This is not the ordinary Way: it involves seizing the very creation of Heaven and Earth, and encroaching on the hidden workings of the sun and moon. Once the elixir is made, devils and spirits cannot tolerate it. Although it will preserve the youthfulness of your face and prolong your life, in five hundred years' time Heaven will strike you with a thunderbolt. You must be clear-sighted in nature and mind, so that you can hide from it before it comes. If you succeed in avoiding it you will live as long as Heaven; and if you don't, it will kill you. Another five hundred years later Heaven will burn you with fire. This fire will be not heavenly fire or ordinary fire but 'hidden fire'. It will burn you from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head; your five viscera will be reduced to ashes, your four limbs will be destroyed, and a thousand years of asceticism will have been so much wasted time. Yet another five hundred years later a wind will blow at you. It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? The Monkey King was the sort of person who understands everything once he is told a tiny part, and he learned the spells on the spot. He practiced and trained until he had mastered all seventy-two transformations.

translation:
Three years had passed, and the Master once again ascended the Precious Seat, discoursing with the assembly. He spoke of case studies and illustrations, discussing external appearances and inner realities. Suddenly, he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong stepped forward and knelt, “Disciple is here.” The Master said, “What path have you been cultivating all this while?” Sun Wukong replied, “Disciple’s nature has become quite clear, and his foundation has grown increasingly solid.” The Master said, “Since you understand the nature and have grasped the root, having already cultivated the divine body, you are only focusing on guarding against the ‘Three Calamities.’” Upon hearing this, Sun Wukong pondered for a long time before saying, “Master, your words are mistaken. I have always heard that those of great virtue live long lives, sharing the longevity of heaven, traversing water and fire unharmed, and immune to a hundred diseases. Yet, how can there be such things as the ‘Three Calamities’?”

The Master said, “This is an extraordinary path: to seize the transformations of heaven and earth, to violate the profound mysteries of the sun and moon; after the elixir is formed, spirits and gods will find it unbearable. Although your appearance will be preserved, and your lifespan extended, after five hundred years, heavenly lightning will strike you. You must then realize your true nature and illuminate your mind in order to avoid it. If you evade it, your lifespan will be equal to heaven’s. If not, you will perish. Another five hundred years later, a fire disaster will descend from heaven. This is not heavenly fire nor mortal fire, but ‘Yin Fire.’ It will rise from the wellspring beneath your body, penetrating the earthen chamber palace, turning your five viscera into ashes and your limbs into decay, turning your thousand years of ascetic practice into a mere illusion. Five hundred years later, a wind disaster will descend. This is not the wind of the four cardinal directions, nor the wind of sunrise and sunset, nor the wind of flowers, willows, pines, and bamboos, but ‘Bi Feng.’ It will blow into your six internal organs from the fontanelle opening, pass through your dantian, pierce your nine orifices, causing your flesh and bones to loosen, and your body to disintegrate. That is why you must avoid them all.”

Upon hearing this, Sun Wukong shivered, bowed his head in reverence, and said, “Great Master, you have shown mercy by revealing the method for avoiding the Three Calamities. I will certainly not forget this kindness.” The Master said, “This is not difficult, but since you are different from others, I cannot pass on the method to you.” Sun Wukong said, “I have a round head, reach to the sky, my feet are square and touch the ground. I have the nine orifices, four limbs, five viscera, and six bowels, just like others. How can I be different?” The Master said, “Although you resemble a human, you lack the cheekbones.” It was indeed true that the monkey had a hollow face, a pointed mouth, and a sunken cheek. Sun Wukong reached out and touched his face, laughing and saying, “Master, you have failed to notice! Although I lack cheekbones, I possess this pouch, and it can also be used for transformation.” The Master said, “Very well, if you wish to learn like an ordinary person, there are thirty-six heavenly transformations and seventy-two earthly transformations. Sun Wukong said, “Disciple is willing to diligently study and master one earthly transformation.” The Master said, “Then come closer and I will impart the secret teachings.” He leaned in close and whispered something unintelligible. This Monkey King, possessing an intelligence that opens all paths, immediately understood the teachings. He practiced and cultivated, mastering all seventy-two earthly transformations.
source_text: 却早过了三年，祖师复登宝座，与众说法。谈的是公案比语，论的是外像包皮。忽问：“悟空何在？”悟空近前跪下：“弟子有。”祖师道：“你这一向修些什么道来？”悟空道：“弟子近来法性颇通，根源亦渐坚固矣。”祖师道：“你既通法性，会得根源，已注神体，却只是防备着‘三灾利害’。”悟空听说，沉吟良久道：“师父之言谬矣。我常闻道高德隆，与天同寿，水火既济，百病不生，却怎么有个三灾利害？”祖师道：“此乃非常之道：夺天地之造化，侵日月之玄机；丹成之后，鬼神难容。虽驻颜益寿，但到了五百年后，天降雷灾打你，须要见性明心，预先躲避。躲得过，寿与天齐，躲不过，就此绝命。再五百年后，天降火灾烧你。这火不是天火，亦不是凡火，唤做‘阴火’。自本身涌泉穴下烧起，直透泥垣宫，五脏成灰，四肢皆朽，把千年苦行，俱为虚幻。再五百年，又降风灾吹你。这风不是东南西北风，不是和薰金朔风，亦不是花柳松竹风，唤做‘赑风’。自囟门中吹入六腑，过丹田，穿九窍，骨肉消疏，其身自解。所以都要躲过。”悟空闻说，毛骨悚然，叩头礼拜道：“万老爷垂悯，传与躲避三灾之法，到底不敢忘恩。”祖师道：“此亦无难，只是你比他人不同，故传不得。”悟空道：“我也头圆顶天，足方履地，一般有九窍四肢，五脏六腑，何以比人不同？”祖师道：“你虽然像人，却比人少腮。”原来那猴子孤拐面，凹脸尖嘴。悟空伸手一摸，笑道：“师父没成算！我虽少腮，却比人多这个素袋，亦可准折过也。”祖师说：“也罢，你要学那一般？有一般天罡数，该三十六般变化，有一般地煞数，该七十二般变化。”悟空道：“弟子愿多里捞摸，学一个地煞变化罢。”祖师道：“既如此，上前来，传与你口诀。”遂附耳低言，不知说了些甚么妙法。这猴王也是一窍通时百窍通，当时习了口诀，自修自炼，将七十二般变化，都学成了。

human_translations.translator_4: After three years had passed in this way the Patriarch once more sat on his lecturing throne and expounded the Dharma to the students. He recounted famous sayings and parables, and discussed external phenomena and external appearances. Without warning he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong went forward, knelt down and replied, “Your disciple is present.” “What Way have you cultivated since coming here?” “Your disciple is now fairly well conversant with the Dharma,” Sun Wukong replied, “and my Source is getting gradually stronger.” “If you are conversant with the Dharma and you know about the Source,” the Patriarch replied, “and if the spirit has already flowed into you, then you must beware of the 'Three Disasters.'” Sun Wukong thought for a long time, then he said, “Patriarch, you're talking rubbish. I have often heard that the Way is lofty and its power mighty, that it is as eternal as Heaven, that it can overcome fire and water, and prevent all illnesses from arising, so how could there be “Three Disasters?'” To this the Patriarch replied, “This is not the ordinary Way: it involves seizing the very creation of Heaven and Earth, and encroaching on the hidden workings of the sun and moon. Once the elixir is made, devils and spirits cannot tolerate it. Although it will preserve the youthfulness of your face and prolong your life, in five hundred years' time Heaven will strike you with a thunderbolt. You must be clear-sighted in nature and mind, so that you can hide from it before it comes. If you succeed in avoiding it you will live as long as Heaven; and if you don't, it will kill you. Another five hundred years later Heaven will burn you with fire. This fire will be not heavenly fire or ordinary fire but 'hidden fire'. It will burn you from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head; your five viscera will be reduced to ashes, your four limbs will be destroyed, and a thousand years of asceticism will have been so much wasted time. Yet another five hundred years later a wind will blow at you. It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? translation: Three years had passed. The Master ascended the throne once more and spoke to the gathered crowd. He discussed koans and parables, expounding on outward appearances and inner substance. Suddenly, he asked, "Where is Sun Wukong?" Sun Wukong stepped forward and knelt. "Disciple is here." The Master said, "What path have you been cultivating?" Sun Wukong replied, "Disciple's Dharma nature has become quite clear, and my root is growing increasingly solid." The Master said, "Since you've grasped Dharma nature and found your root, you've already entered the realm of the divine body, yet you are merely guarding against the 'three calamities and great dangers.'" Sun Wukong, upon hearing this, pondered for a long time before saying, "Master's words are amiss. I have often heard that those of high virtue live long lives, equal to heaven's, able to pass through fire and water unharmed, free from all ailments. How can there be such a thing as the 'three calamities and great dangers'?" The Master said, "This is an extraordinary path: one that takes away the Heaven's creative force, violating the celestial mysteries. After achieving the elixir, spirits and ghosts find it difficult to approach. Although your appearance may remain youthful, after five hundred years, a heavenly thunderbolt will strike you down. You must attain enlightenment and open your mind beforehand to avoid it. If you manage to evade it, you will live as long as heaven; if not, you will perish. Another five hundred years later, a fire calamity will descend. This fire is not heavenly fire nor mortal fire; it is called 'yin fire.' It will rise from the wellspring below your womb, piercing through the palace walls, turning your five viscera into ash and your limbs into decay, rendering your millennia of ascetic practices illusory. Another five hundred years later, a wind calamity will strike. This wind is not a wind from the east, west, south, or north, nor is it the wind that dries gold, blows back the moon, or rustles through flowers, willows, pines, and bamboos. It is called 'pi feng.' It will blow into your six internal organs from the fontanelle, pass through your dantian, and pierce your nine orifices, causing your flesh and bones to dissipate, leading to your self-dissolution. Thus, you must evade all three." Sun Wukong, upon hearing this, felt a chill run down his spine. He bowed his head in reverence and said, "Great Master, you have shown mercy by revealing the method to avoid the three calamities. I will never forget your kindness." The Master said, "It is not difficult. It is simply that you are different from others, hence I cannot pass on the method directly." Sun Wukong said, "I too have a round head that reaches the heavens, feet that spread wide on the ground, nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six organs. How am I different from others?" The Master said, "Although you resemble a human, you lack cheeks." Indeed, the monkey's face was gaunt, with sunken cheeks and a pointed mouth. Sun Wukong reached out to touch his face and laughed. "Master, you haven't won! Though I lack cheeks, I possess this pouch, which I can also use to transform." The Master said, "Very well, if you wish to learn like an ordinary person, there are thirty-six celestial transformations and seventy-two earthly transformations. " Sun Wukong said, "Disciple wishes to learn one earthly transformation." The Master said, "Very well, come forward and I will impart the mantra."  He leaned in and whispered something profound. This monkey king, having a mind that quickly grasped everything, understood the mantra instantly. After that, he practiced diligently, perfecting all seventy-two earthly transformations.
source_text: 却早过了三年，祖师复登宝座，与众说法。谈的是公案比语，论的是外像包皮。忽问：“悟空何在？”悟空近前跪下：“弟子有。”祖师道：“你这一向修些什么道来？”悟空道：“弟子近来法性颇通，根源亦渐坚固矣。”祖师道：“你既通法性，会得根源，已注神体，却只是防备着‘三灾利害’。”悟空听说，沉吟良久道：“师父之言谬矣。我常闻道高德隆，与天同寿，水火既济，百病不生，却怎么有个三灾利害？”祖师道：“此乃非常之道：夺天地之造化，侵日月之玄机；丹成之后，鬼神难容。虽驻颜益寿，但到了五百年后，天降雷灾打你，须要见性明心，预先躲避。躲得过，寿与天齐，躲不过，就此绝命。再五百年后，天降火灾烧你。这火不是天火，亦不是凡火，唤做‘阴火’。自本身涌泉穴下烧起，直透泥垣宫，五脏成灰，四肢皆朽，把千年苦行，俱为虚幻。再五百年，又降风灾吹你。这风不是东南西北风，不是和薰金朔风，亦不是花柳松竹风，唤做‘赑风’。自囟门中吹入六腑，过丹田，穿九窍，骨肉消疏，其身自解。所以都要躲过。”悟空闻说，毛骨悚然，叩头礼拜道：“万老爷垂悯，传与躲避三灾之法，到底不敢忘恩。”祖师道：“此亦无难，只是你比他人不同，故传不得。”悟空道：“我也头圆顶天，足方履地，一般有九窍四肢，五脏六腑，何以比人不同？”祖师道：“你虽然像人，却比人少腮。”原来那猴子孤拐面，凹脸尖嘴。悟空伸手一摸，笑道：“师父没成算！我虽少腮，却比人多这个素袋，亦可准折过也。”祖师说：“也罢，你要学那一般？有一般天罡数，该三十六般变化，有一般地煞数，该七十二般变化。”悟空道：“弟子愿多里捞摸，学一个地煞变化罢。”祖师道：“既如此，上前来，传与你口诀。”遂附耳低言，不知说了些甚么妙法。这猴王也是一窍通时百窍通，当时习了口诀，自修自炼，将七十二般变化，都学成了。

He discussed the scholastic deliberations and parables, and he discoursed on the integument of external conduct. I was a child... but the meaning was probably that! Napoleon was impressed; he pondered and said to his retinue: "I admire the pride of this child! source_text: «Русское сердце в состоянии даже в самом враге своего отечества отличить великого человека!». В свите уже расступались предо мной и смотрели на меня как на фаворита. Но всё это только мелькнуло... Помню только, что, войдя в первую залу, император вдруг остановился пред портретом императрицы Екатерины, долго, смотрел на него в задумчивости и наконец произнес: «Это была великая женщина!» — и прошел мимо. Чрез два дня меня все уже знали во дворце и в Кремле и звали «le petit boyard». Я только ночевать уходил домой. Дома чуть с ума не сошли. Еще чрез два дня умирает камер-паж Наполеона, барон де Базанкур, не вынесший похода. Наполеон вспомнил обо мне; меня взяли, привели, не объясняя дела, примерили на меня мундир покойного, мальчика лет двенадцати, и, когда уже привели меня в мундире к императору и он кивнул на меня головой, объявили мне, что я удостоен милостью и произведен в камер-пажи его величества. Я был рад, я действительно чувствовал к нему, и давно уже, горячую симпатию... ну, и кроме того, согласитесь, блестящий мундир, что для ребенка составляет многое... Я ходил в темно-зеленом фраке, с длинными и узкими фалдами; золотые пуговицы, красные опушки на рукавах с золотым шитьем, высокий, стоячий, открытый воротник, шитый золотом, шитье на фалдах; белые лосинные панталоны в обтяжку, белый шелковый жилет, шелковые чулки, башмаки с пряжками... а во время прогулок императора на коне, и если я участвовал в свите, высокие ботфорты. Хотя положение было не блестящее и предчувствовались уже огромные бедствия, но этикет соблюдался по возможности, и даже тем пунктуальнее, чем сильнее предчувствовались эти бедствия.

translation:
The next day, three court officials, gathered with monks, in that mountain and river hall, one by one searched from the beginning, and selected a high-ranking monk with good conduct. You ask who he is? His original name was Jinguichan, but he only wished to have no heart to listen to the Buddha's teachings, and instead, he bore the suffering of the mundane world, reincarnating into the world of mortals and falling into the snare of fate. At birth, he encountered danger, before even being born, his life threatened by evil forces. His father was Chen Zhuangyuan of Haizhou, and his great-uncle was the chief minister of the current dynasty. Born under the ill omen of the Falling River Star, he drifted with the current like a leaf on the water. On a large island with golden mountains, he was raised by Master Qian'an. At eighteen, he recognized his biological mother and went to the capital to seek out his great-uncle. The chief minister, Yin Kaisan, raised an army and quelled bandits in Hongzhou. Zhuangyuan Guangru'i escaped the heavenly net, and father and son met, a cause for celebration and reward. Then he visited the current emperor to express his gratitude and received honor on the Lingyan Pavilion, his virtuous name echoing throughout the ages. Though offered official positions, he declined, choosing instead to become a monk, seeking the path of enlightenment. He was known as Chen Xuanzang, the "Ancient Buddha's Son of the River," his Dharma name. On that day, the three officials presented Xuanzang to the court.

This man had been a monk since childhood, taking monastic vows even before leaving his mother's womb. His great-uncle was Yin Kaisan, the chief minister, and his father, Chen Guangru'i, was a scholar and served as Minister of the Ministry of Rites. Yet he had no love for wealth and honor, only a passion for practicing meditation and tranquility. When they discovered his innate disposition and his high morality, they found him to be profound in understanding, knowledgeable in scriptures: Buddha's pronouncements were like fairy music to him, and he mastered all teachings. 

The three officials then led him before the emperor, bowing and dancing. After completing the dance, they declared: "We, your ministers, have been ordered to select a high-ranking monk. The chosen one is Chen Xuanzang." Emperor Taizong pondered upon his name for a long time and asked, "Is he the son of scholar Chen Guangru'i, Xuanzang?" Xuanzang bowed and replied, "Yes, Your Majesty, it is I." The emperor rejoiced, saying, "Indeed, a good choice, a monk with both virtue and a true heart. I bestow upon you the positions of Left Chief Abbot, Right Chief Abbot, and Chief Abbot of the Great Chan Monastery." Xuanzang bowed deeply in gratitude and accepted the honorific titles. He was further bestowed with a five-colored silk and gold kasaya robe and a jeweled hat.

The emperor instructed him to go to the Ming Seng Monastery, take his place at the head of the hierarchy of monks, and to prepare for the upcoming Water and Land Buddhist gathering. He also ordered that a detailed schedule be drawn up and sent to the monastery. Xuanzang bowed to accept the imperial decree and departed to the Ming Seng Monastery. There, he gathered monks, prepared meditation cushions, renovated the temple grounds, and arranged musical performances. A total of 1,200 monks were selected and assigned to three halls: upper, middle, and lower. Everything before the Buddha was in perfect order, with each item in its proper place. The auspicious day was set for the beginning of the Water and Land assembly on the third day of the first lunar month, during a favorable time according to astrological calculations. 

Emperor Taizong, along with the ministers, high officials, princes, and nobles, all attended the grand gathering, offering incense and listening to the teachings. What would the emperor's ultimate intentions be? We will learn this in the next installment.
source_text: 次日，三位朝臣，聚众僧，在那山川坛里，逐一从头查选，内中选得一名有德行的高僧。你道他是谁人？灵通本讳号金蝉，只为无心听佛讲，转托尘凡苦受磨，降生世俗遭罗网。投胎落地就逢凶，未出之前临恶党。父是海州陈状元，外公总管当朝长。出身命犯落江星，顺水随波逐浪泱。海岛金山有大缘，迁安和尚将他养。年方十八认亲娘，特赴京都求外长。总管开山调大军，洪州剿寇诛凶党。状元光蕊脱天罗，子父相逢堪贺奖。复谒当今受主恩，凌烟阁上贤名响。恩官不受愿为僧，洪福沙门将道访。小字江流古佛儿，法名唤做陈玄奘。当日对众举出玄奘法师。这个人自幼为僧，出娘胎，就持斋受戒。他外公见是当朝一路总管殷开山，他父亲陈光蕊，中状元，官拜文渊殿大学士。一心不爱荣华，只喜修持寂灭。查得他根源又好，德行又高。千经万典，无所不通：佛号仙音，无般不会。当时三位引至御前，扬尘舞蹈，拜罢奏曰：“臣瑀等蒙圣旨，选得高僧一名陈玄奘。”太宗闻其名，沉思良久道：“可是学士陈光蕊之儿玄奘否？”江流儿叩头曰：“臣正是。”太宗喜道：“果然举之不错，诚为有德行有禅心的和尚。朕赐你左僧纲、右僧纲、天下大阐都僧纲之职。”玄奘顿首谢恩，受了大阐官爵。又赐五彩织金袈裟一件，毗卢帽一顶。教他用心再拜明僧，排次阇黎班首，书办旨意，前赴化生寺，择定吉日良时，开演经法。玄奘再拜领旨而出，遂到化生寺里，聚集多僧，打造禅榻，装修功德，整理音乐。选得大小明僧共计一千二百名，分派上中下三堂。诸所佛前，物件皆齐，头头有次。选到本年九月初三日，黄道良辰，开启做七七四十九日水陆大会。即具表申奏，太宗及文武国戚皇亲，俱至期赴会，拈香听讲。毕竟不知圣意如何，且听下回分解。

At the age of eighteen, he recognized his mother and went to Kyoto to seek foreign minister. The general manager opened up the mountain to transfer the army, and Hongzhou suppressed the bandits and executed the murderous party.
